notes.title: Version 1.9.0 Release
notes.notes:
Version 1.9 features performance improvements for editor preview visualizations. Enabling these previews could cause significant delays in the graph editor, especially when working with large 3d meshes. This update brings a level-of-detail solution that significantly reduces these delays.
As a second change, a loading screen for graphs is now shown during application startup. It is now possible to select the correct workspace(s) to load. In older versions, all workspaces were loaded. This could make it impossible to start procedural studio if a file was corrupted

notes.title: Small Usability Update
notes.notes:
It is now possible to copy a selection of nodes via copy-and-paste buttons or keyboard shortcuts. All connections and open input parameters of the selection will be identical in the copy. This update also includes some polishing of UI elements as well as some smaller bugfixes.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45170563/ff910e698f11cfd1f46a44a3dff100968c328fa3.png

notes.title: Release 1.7.0
notes.notes:
Version 1.7.0 of Procedural Studio features preview visualizations of node results directly in the graph editor. This includes direct previews of functions (1D, 2D and 3D) as well as images and meshes (2D and 3D). In some cases, this visualization can slow down the performance, so a toggle button was added to enable or disable the previews, depending on your system and the size of your data. In addition to the previews, a "fit view" button was added to the editor toolbar to fit the full graph into the editor frame. Furthermore, several bugs have been fixed.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45170563/095796374473dab4e44a0635de25c45b4727074a.png

notes.title: New Exporting Options (1.6.0 Release)
notes.notes:
Saving images was limited to 8 bit pixel format which is not suitable for heightmaps. Version 1.6.0 brings you a set of new features for exporting grayscale images and heightmaps. The following are all changes in detail:
* The new node "Save Heightmap" features 16 bit exports of grayscale images (heightmaps). It supports three different file formats.
* The new node "Tiled Heightmap Export" also supports 16 bit data and works similar to the existing "Tiled Export" for 8 bit rgba images.
* Polished all exporting ui widgets for better usability of filename selection.
* Demo Version: Downscaling of images during export now preserves the aspect ratio.
* Several small bugs related to saving and exporting have been fixed.

notes.title: Procedural Studio 1.5.0 Release
notes.notes:
Version 1.5.0 contains small usability improvements and important bugfixes.
These are the changes in detail:

 Ordering of inputs and outputs of nodes is no longer alphabetical. The inputs and outputs of nodes are now logically grouped. For example, width and height parameters, or x and y parameters, are now grouped logically instead of alphabetically
 The colorscale editor is now initialized with a color, and the current color gradient is shown in the parameter-editor button.
 Node-blocks for subgraphs are now shown with a thicker line width.
 Default input parameter ranges have been adjusted for several nodes.
 Node selection visualization has been changed.
 Several minor bugs (and one or two major bugs) have been fixed.

notes.title: Usability Update
notes.notes:
Procedural Studio version 1.3.0 was just released. This update features a rework of the node editor. Numerical inputs of nodes can now be set and adjusted using sliders with a variable range.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45170563/b3b53f9e7ca3ea9c14fe7366d48c308931dfd7a3.png

The following is a summary of all changes in detail:
1) The layout of the node editor window has been changed: Parameter names are now listed on the left; values are displayed on the right side of the widget. Separator lines have been included between different parameter controls. The border has been removed from the editor area.
2) Numerical inputs can now be set via sliders.
3) The range of the sliders can be manually adjusted using two additional input fields on the left and right side of the slider.
4) Bugfixes in Random Real, Random Uniform, and Random Gaussian number generators that could cause crashes.
5) Curvature Map and Occlusion map nodes: Strength parameter has no influence and has been marked obsolete.

notes.title: New Update Available
notes.notes:
The following 8 changes have been implemented:
1) The connection editor now works with a catch range, making it easier to hit input ports with the cursor. The catch range area is highlighted in green or red, depending on whether the connection is possible.
2) The new image processing node Inverter inverts the colors of an input image.
3) The new image processing nodes Crop (Pixels) and Crop (Relative) provide more convenient ways to crop an input image.
4) The new image processing node Select Color selects the areas of an input image that have a specific color.
5) Hitting the spacebar now executes the graph, making it easier to adjust values without having to move the mouse cursor to the execute-button.
6) Bugfix: Default values for color-value open inputs are now correctly initialized in the color-editor window.
7) Bugfix: Single-channel images are now always visualized in black-and-white, as specified in the last update version 1.1.0
8) Bugfix: The 3D Function viewer now displays the correct message text.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45170563/517e0ef896e74eb740141bc2abbf1ce0983cc3ad.png
The image shows the catch-range feature in the graph editor

notes.title: Small Usability Update
notes.notes:
Three minor changes have been implemented with version 1.1.0:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45170563/94a369ab9da86916e09ef9c9180e56fe71193294.png


 The node description pop-up window now shows the color codes for parameter types, making it easier to identify nodes with the right connections.
 Single-Channel images are now displayed in black-and-white instead of in a red color.
 The node category "Basic" has been renamed to "Misc" and the tab is moved to the bottom of the widget

notes.title: Public Release!
notes.notes:
Version 1.0.0 of Procedural Studio is out now. Try the free demo today!

The software does have a learning curve, so make sure to check out the user guide and examples at www.proceduralstudio.org

Feedback and feature suggestions are welcome! Contact me via Steam or head over to reddit.com/r/proceduralstudio to start a discussion on my subreddit.

Have a great weekend!
